records.issue_text: ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException but is called unconditionally by AdminPermissions.registerListener on ClientRemovedEvent, causing a 500 error and failed client deletion in V2 realms with ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ enabled
records.rationale: In `AdminPermissions.registerListener`, when `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` is enabled it unconditionally handles `ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent` by calling `management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false)`. In this diff, `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` returns `ClientPermissionsV2`, and `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(...)` is implemented as `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")`. Therefore, under V2 permissions, a `ClientRemovedEvent` would trigger an exception during listener handling, consistent with a 500/error path.

records.rationale: In PermissionClientTest.testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient the test creates two client roles with fixed names ("myclient-role" and "myclient-subRole") via realm.admin().clients().get(myclient.getId()).roles().create(...), but the added @AfterEach cleanup in PermissionClientTest only removes scope permissions (permissions.findAll(...).forEach(...remove())) and does not delete those roles/composites.
